messages:
tori: hit a reproducible hang in the go generator sample when cancelling a long-lived stream. ctrl-C returns from Generate but process stays up. pprof shows a goroutine blocked in auth refresh network call.

ben: can you share the minimal repro?

tori: pared down version from our demo: 
```go
func run(ctx context.Context) {
  go authLoop() // background refresh using old TokenSource
  client.Generate(ctx, req) // streaming generator
}

func authLoop() {
  for {
    token := blockingFetch() // no ctx-aware http request
    time.Sleep(time.Minute)
  }
}
```

tori: behavior: after sending SIGINT, Generate returns (we cancel ctx) but process remains because blockingFetch never returns.

oli: sounds like onboarding friction: sampleapp implies ctx cancellation suffices, but legacy token refreshs block.

ben: short fixes: update sampleapp to use signal.NotifyContext and demonstrate wrapping a legacy TokenSource with a cancellable adapter. long-term: add a Refresh(ctx) variant or an adapter in the go SDK.

tori: i'll open a tiny sampleapp PR demonstrating the adapter and add a note in the onboarding README: "If your auth refresh blocks, wrap it to respect ctx when running long-lived streams."

oli: also add a unit test that uses a net/http test server that accepts connections and stalls to simulate the blocked refresh; that should catch regressions.

ci-bot: Created ticket RW-7701: "go-sdk: adapter for context-aware token refresh + sampleapp update" and kicked off a workflow.

ben: nice. remember to include a small test that asserts process exits within a few seconds after cancel. tori: ping me on the PR for a review.

tori: will do, thanks!
